steps.tx: **Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma** accounts for over **90%** of all pancreatic malignancies, characterized by dense desmoplasia and early vascular invasion. Its molecular pathogenesis is initiated by activating **KRAS mutations** in codon 12, present in over **90%** of tumors. This is followed by sequential inactivating mutations in major tumor suppressor genes: CDKN2A/p**16** in over 90%, TP**53** in 70%, and SMAD**4**/DPC4 in 55%, driving progression from microscopic PanIN lesions to metastatic cancer.

steps.tx: Carbohydrate antigen **CA 19-9** is the primary validated serum biomarker for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, widely utilized to assess therapeutic response and detect post-resection recurrence. However, CA 19-9 is a sialylated **Lewis blood group** antigen (sialyl Lewis-a). Approximately **5%** to **10%** of the general population are homozygous for the null Lewis phenotype (Le a-b-) due to inactivating mutations in the fucosyltransferase enzyme FUT**3**, rendering CA 19-9 synthesis biochemically impossible.

rows: Falsely elevated; recheck after biliary drainage
Indicates early local or distant recurrence

steps.tx: **Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms** are mucin-producing cystic tumors that communicate directly with the pancreatic ductal system. Under the revised international **Fukuoka guidelines**, surgical resection is strongly indicated when high-risk stigmata are present. High-risk stigmata comprise clinical obstructive jaundice in a patient with a cystic lesion of the pancreatic head, an enhancing solid mural nodule measuring at least **5** mm, or a main pancreatic duct diameter of at least **10** mm.
steps.say: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, or IPMN, are mucin-producing cystic tumors that communicate directly with the pancreatic ductal system. Under the revised international Fukuoka guidelines, surgical resection is strongly indicated when high-risk stigmata are present. High-risk stigmata comprise clinical obstructive jaundice in a patient with a cystic lesion of the pancreatic head, an enhancing solid mural nodule measuring at least 5 mm, or a main pancreatic duct diameter of at least 10 mm.

left.title: High-Risk Stigmata (Mandates Resection)
points: Obstructive jaundice with pancreatic head cyst

right.title: Worrisome Features (Warrants EUS Evaluation)
points: Main pancreatic duct calibre 5 to 9.9 mm

steps.tx: **Mucinous cystic neoplasms** occur almost exclusively in middle-aged perimenopausal women, located predominantly in the pancreatic body or tail (**90%** of cases). They do not communicate with the pancreatic ductal system. Pathognomonic histopathological confirmation requires identifying dense, cellular subepithelial **ovarian-type stroma** staining positive for estrogen and progesterone receptors. Cyst fluid aspiration characteristically demonstrates thick viscous mucin with markedly elevated CEA exceeding **192** ng/mL.

steps.tx: **Serous cystadenomas** are entirely benign neoplasms that carry virtually no malignant potential. Cross-sectional imaging reveals a characteristic microcystic **honeycomb morphology** composed of myriad tiny cysts separated by thin fibrous septa, often coalescing around a central stellate calcified scar. Aspiration of thin, watery cyst fluid confirms an extremely low CEA level below **5** ng/mL and absent mucin. On biopsy, the cysts are lined by uniform, glycogen-rich cuboidal epithelial cells.

nodes.label: Microcystic honeycomb lesion with central stellate scar
Cyst fluid analysis: CEA < 5 ng/mL and amylase low

steps.tx: **Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm** is a distinctive low-grade malignant epithelial neoplasm occurring almost exclusively in young women in their second or third decade of life. Driven by activating mutations in the **beta-catenin** gene CTNNB**1**, tumors exhibit nuclear and cytoplasmic accumulation of beta-catenin with loss of membranous E-cadherin. Lesions are well-circumscribed mixed solid and cystic masses with areas of haemorrhage, and complete surgical resection is typically curative.

right.title: Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
points: Demographic: Elderly men and women (mean age 65-70)
Genetics: KRAS, TP53, CDKN2A, SMAD4 mutations

steps.tx: Advances in precision oncology have identified therapeutic vulnerabilities in subsets of pancreatic neuroendocrine and ductal tumors. Approximately five to seven percent of pancreatic adenocarcinomas harbor germline or somatic BRCA**1** or BRCA**2** mutations, resulting in deficient homologous recombination repair. In the phase III **POLO trial**, maintenance monotherapy with the oral PARP inhibitor **olaparib** significantly prolonged progression-free survival in metastatic patients whose disease had not progressed on first-line platinum chemotherapy.

Switch to maintenance PARP inhibitor Olaparib (POLO protocol)

steps.tx: **Insulinoma** represents the most prevalent functioning pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, characterized by autonomous insulin secretion that induces profound fasting neuroglycopenia. Diagnosis is suspected via **Whipple triad**: symptoms of hypoglycemia, documented plasma venous glucose below **55** mg/dL, and rapid symptom resolution following glucose administration. Confirmation requires a supervised **72**-hour inpatient fast demonstrating inappropriately elevated serum insulin, C-peptide, and proinsulin levels during hypoglycemia.
